coverage.found: English search returned only foreign regimes. No Cypriot second-hand/pawnbroker licensing law or register found. Greek terms (ενεχυροδανειστές, μεταχειρισμένα) not searched. Unverified.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Only the EU ELV Directive 2000/53 framework came up (permitted treatment facilities issue certificates of destruction). The Cypriot transposing law and register were not found.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Veterinary Services runs a central ovine/caprine database (since 2002), so the state holds the register. No trader-level duty found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Butcheries register once with the Veterinary Services (KDP 377/2009, HACCP manual, €80 fee, no expiry, inspections). No recurring filing. Abattoir licensing rules not found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No Cypriot apiary registration rule found. Eurostat shows about 33,640 hives on holdings in 2023. Nothing found to build on.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary Medicines and Medicated Feed law (2022 bill), and a wholesale authorisation form on businessincyprus.gov.cy that requires daily temperature/humidity logs. Retail dispensing records and any central reporting duty not checked.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Search returned only Water Development Department reports. No borehole licence, metering or reporting duty confirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Waste collectors/transporters must be in the Waste Managers Registry and use an Identification and Monitoring Form (OEB presentation; Waste Law 185(I)/2011). Septic-sludge specific rules not found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Lift owners must have a periodic inspection at least every 24 months (Regs 533/2012 as amended by 232/2023; TUV Cyprus page). Boiler/pressure-vessel inspection duty not confirmed.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Only the EU DWD 2020/2184 and a 2024 national water investment plan. Local government reform (Law 37(I)/2022, in effect 1 July 2024) may have moved supply duties. Unverified.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Agricultural pesticide seller licence under the Agricultural Pesticides (Sale, Preparation, Storage) Regulations 2003, with licence forms replaced by a 2024 order (cylaw 2024_1_337). The PDF could not be parsed. Dealer record-keeping and sprayer certification not found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Private Employment Agencies licence is renewed through the Department of Labour (form on businessincyprus.gov.cy). Amending law was in parliament in 2022. Third-country worker employment is governed by Aliens and Immigration Law Cap.105 and 7(I)/2019. Recurring reporting not confirmed.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: A secondary Q&A says funeral services need a licence and cemeteries are governed by local authorities (2004 law, number unverified). Nothing official found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations and Foundations Law 2017 and 2020 regulations (forms, fees). Annual financial filing duty not confirmed. No halal/kosher body found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi licensing reform package (POS, end of off-book licence rental, driver refresher training) due at the Transport Ministry end-Nov 2025, still a proposal. Illegal operators fined €700 since July 2024. 246 rural and 1,556 urban taxi licences. Passenger transport regulation bill 2024 exists.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Not directly searched beyond the business-sector list, which has no money changer or street vendor category. Nothing found.

coverage.found: Driving schools: Motor Vehicles (Drivers Training) Law 112/1968, licence valid 1 year (renewal €17.09), no records duty found. Nurseries: Greek results only, Cypriot rules not found. Tattoo and hunting outfitters not searched.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Station licence is issued by the municipality or District Officer, with a Public Works certificate under Petroleum Law Cap 272 and a Fire Service report (businessincyprus.gov.cy petrol-station page). Only 2026 items are a July 2026 owners' protest over a transport-ministry tanker decree and Petrolina/ExxonMobil divestments. No recurring small-operator reporting duty found. LPG distributor rules not found (unverified).

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No search spent. Cyprus has no coffee or cocoa trade, and grain/carob/halloumi traders were not checked within budget.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operative societies are supervised by a separate authority and credit co-operatives by the Central Bank. The search found no source on annual-return or register duties for small co-operatives. Cooperative sector is being consolidated, with a new co-operative bank under discussion (cyprus-mail Nov 2024). Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: GESY/HIO is the single payer. HIO rejected about 80,000 claims worth EUR 10m, fined 30 providers EUR 100-30,000, terminated contracts and reported 9 cases to police (cyprus-mail 2024-02-16, fetched). Barcode e-prescriptions since 2026-03-27. Claim-submission rules and any approved-software list not found. See candidate C03.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacies are inside GESY; handwritten specialised-drug prescriptions invalid from 2025-05-15 and barcode scan from 2026-03-27. EU falsified-medicines traceability is likely to apply but no Cyprus source found (unverified). Nothing new beyond C03 buyer overlap.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No land-guard or cleaning-agency licence register confirmed. Employer duty to update foreign-worker details on a national platform one day before start, with EUR 1,000 per undeclared worker fines, rising with repeats (Fragomen Jun 2025 via search snippet; fetch blocked 403; cyprus-mail 2026-05-07). See C04.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Contractors are licensed annually by a Council for Registration and Control of Contractors, with a technical director and class limits. From 2026-03-11 building-permit applications need full mechanical-installation studies, supervision by the design engineer and completion certificates from mechanical and electrical engineers, now including single-family homes; ETEK register of design/supervising engineers mandatory from July 2028 (cyprus-mail 2026-03-18, fetched). See C01.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Cyprus has no notaries; lawyers do conveyancing. 2026 draft AML amendment moves real-estate supervision from the Real Estate Agents Registration Council to the Tax Department, with the new supervisor expected operational by July 2027 (mondaq 1735176, fetched; enactment not confirmed). Lawyers/ASPs fall under K07. See C02.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03. New evidence: register held 8,464 licensed self-catering units on 2026-05-06; Audit Office found 50% of a sample without valid number; ministry drafting law with mandatory safety certificates and on-site inspections (dom.com.cy, fetched). Reg. 2024/1028 applies from 2026-05-20.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). EUDR/timber/fish importers not checked.

coverage.category: 31. Engineering design and building-installation offices (ETEK-registered)
coverage.found: March 2026 mechanical-installation rules and ETEK register, see C01 and K01.

coverage.category: 32. Land-based betting shops and agents (National Betting Authority, Law 37(I)/2019)
coverage.found: Class A licences; NBA publishes licence non-renewals (Bookieco expired 2026-02-09 and its agents' premises must stop). Shop count shrinking. NBA directives on quarterly reporting and self-exclusion cited by a law-firm blog are unconfirmed. See C07.

coverage.category: 33. Packaging producers and small importers (Green Dot Cyprus EPR, PPWR)
coverage.found: Annual packaging declaration to Green Dot Cyprus by end of February; Green Dot audits about 20 members a year; PPWR (EU 2025/40) applies from 2026-08-12, Cyprus procedure for authorised representatives and producer register unpublished, Department of Environment guidance announced for September 2026 (wko.at, fetched). See C05.

coverage.category: 34. Refrigeration/air-conditioning technicians and F-gas equipment operators
coverage.found: Certification body is the Department of Environment (old regulation KDP 133/2010); EU Reg. 2024/573 now applies with an F-gas portal. No current Cyprus register or leak-log rule found. See C06.

coverage.category: 35. Tobacco and e-cigarette retailers
coverage.found: Governed by Health Protection (Smoking Control) Law 24/2017; a regime revision is flagged for 2025-26 by ECigIntelligence. No licence or retailer register found. See C08.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Cyprus Grain Commission was dissolved by Order KDP 156/2021 (Apr 2021), so no state licensing or miller-return regime remains (the 1940s-50s miller register and monthly-return orders are historical only). It is replaced by the Law on Conservation of Feed and Cereal Raw Material Stocks for Human Use 39(I)/2021, with annual Ministerial decrees (KDP 93/2025 of 31.03.2025; a 2026 decree after a Council of Ministers decision of 03.04.2026). These fix the stock quantities per commodity for importers, distributors and major users, and the competent authority holds the strategic stock. Records under the law are used only for its purposes and published only in aggregate. The duty falls on a small number of large importers and mills (Cyprus Millers has 16 silos). It is not a quiet-SME market and the filing form and deadlines were not confirmed. Animal feed intermediaries (anyone who packages, stores or sells feed) need a Registration or Approval Certificate from the Department of Agriculture (businessincyprus.gov.cy); medicated feed distribution needs a separate Veterinary Services authorisation. Seed marketing needs a Department of Agriculture licence. No record or reporting duty specific to these was confirmed. Carob exports are tiny (about EUR 1.8M in 2021); no coffee or cocoa trade. No candidate scores 4 or more.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Timber is the one concrete lead. Law 139(I)/2013 (Control of Trade in Timber and Timber Products) requires an annual timber trading licence (forms T.D. 225/226) and a separate annual firewood trading licence (T.D. 227/228) from the Director of the Department of Forests. Under Art. 8(3) and 9(3) each licence holder must keep a purchase and sales register: supplier, origin, species with Latin name, quantity, buyer ('IK' for private sale), updated immediately, balance reconcilable at any time, kept 5 years, and available to the Director on request. Fines are low (EUR 1,000 for register failures; up to EUR 40,000 or 2 years for missing due diligence or false data). The Department's leaflet still cites EUTR 995/2010 and covers paper, furniture and prefab houses; it is dated about 2013-14. The EUDR (Reg. 2023/1115, amended by Reg. 2025/2650) applies from 30 Dec 2026 to large and medium operators and traders and from 30 Jun 2027 to micro and small ones (per secondary sources, with the delay possibly not covering EUTR products, which would include timber; unverified). Traders that are SMEs mostly gather information and act on substantiated concerns; non-SME traders must register in the EU information system. The CCCI/EEN ran EUDR information-system webinars in Dec 2025. A third-party list names the Department of Forests as the EUDR competent authority; I found no Cyprus implementing law. Fish: IUU catch certificates go through the EU CATCH system, mandatory for importers from 10 Jan 2026 (Reg. 2023/2842). The Cyprus importer registration process was not found and no local tool exists. Halloumi PDO: the Ministry of Agriculture has a certification control plan covering producers, processors, packers, storers and traders; record-keeping details were not read. No local software for any of these was seen.

result.reason: A 24-month lift inspection cycle in Cyprus is supported only by a 2013 consumer-association notice. It says the Department of Labour Inspection (DLI) requires inspection every 24 months from 31/08/2013, by an authorised inspector (Cyprus Certification Company, KEP). The owner then posts an "inspection successful" sticker. I could not read the 2022/2023 amending regulations (the PDFs were unreadable) and found no penalty amounts. I found no Cypriot reminder software, only foreign industrial-lifting tools. The DLI publishes lists of approved maintainers and inspectors, but I did not find an owner-level register. The market size (number of lifts) was not found. Buyers are fragmented building committees paying little, and the inspection firms already schedule the visits, so willingness to pay is low.

The duty is real. Waste collectors and transporters must register in the Waste Management Operators Register under Law 185(I)/2011, and they report through the state's Electronic Waste Registry (ΗΜΑ, ewr.moa.gov.cy). The registry was set up by Decree KDP 312/2020, and the 2024 annual reports were due by 31 March 2025 with no extensions. The state portal is free and already covers the core job, so a third-party product would only add a layer on top of it. The market looks small (probably tens to low hundreds of hauliers). I did not find penalty amounts, haulier counts, a septic-specific permit, or any private competitor, and I did not open the portal itself. The claim's premise of paper forms looks outdated.

result.competitor: None found; not exhaustively searched. Ippodamos is the state planning portal and I could not confirm it has an MEP module.
result.duty: Regulations KDP 129/2026 (11.03.2026) require full mechanical-installation studies, supervision and completion certificates. Penalties and frequency were not confirmed. Register mandatory from July 2028.
result.market: Not quantified. The number of ETEK-registered mechanical and electrical engineers and design offices was not found.
result.reason: The duty looks real. ETEK announced that Regulations KDP 129/2026 were published on 11.03.2026, amending the mechanical and electrical installation rules for buildings. ETEK circular 05/2026 covers transitional provisions, including single-family homes. Cyprus Mail reports a mandatory ETEK register of design and supervising engineers from July 2028. But this is a one-off rule change for engineers, not a recurring filing. No penalties are stated, and I could not read the regulation text (the PDF would not parse). I found no dedicated software or ETEK app for these studies and certificates. The search was thin, though, and I did not check Ippodamos modules. The buyer is a small group of engineers who already have CAD tools. Willingness to pay is low and it is not recurring. Score is 3.

Duty exists today: real estate agents are obliged persons under AML law 188(I)/2007, supervised by the Real Estate Agents Registration Council. The Tax Department move is only a 2026 draft. Public consultation ran to 14 Feb 2026 (one source says 15 Jul 2026). I found no evidence it passed. The July 2027 date comes from the EU 2024/1624 AMLR and a law-firm estimate, not from enacted Cyprus law. Agent count is not found; the 1,000+ figure is unverified. Competition was only partly checked (3 searches): no Cyprus agent-specific AML product turned up, but generic KYC vendors exist (AML Watcher, Cyprus Mail KYC article). Score stays 3: the new supervisor is not live until 2027, the buyers are tiny and fragmented, and generic KYC tools cover the same work. Related to K07.

The enforcement duty is real: HIO audits, rejected claims and fines on GESY providers. Politis reports €231,300 in fines on 49 providers (Jan 2025 to Jun 2026). The claim's 80,000 rejected claims (€10m) figure comes from Cyprus Mail 2024. I could not verify the claim route. Claims go through the HIO's own GESY system, which is state-run and under a contract dispute. A Strategic Plan 2024-2026 mentions APIs to third-party systems, but no open API or approved-vendor list was found. I found no Cyprus GESY clinic-software vendor, but that is unproven. The pain looks like a clinic-software feature, not a standalone product. The buyer is fragmented, there is no per-provider filing deadline, and the dependence on HIO integration is a risk. I did not check the market size or the penalty basis in law, and the 2026 barcode-prescription date was not confirmed.

The duty is real. Law 32(I)/2002 requires producers to join an approved system, and Green Dot Cyprus is the only approved packaging PRO. Members declare by the end of February, and penalties reach 3 years or EUR 85,000 (Lappa, a consultancy, so secondary). No Cyprus-specific software was found, but I ran no dedicated vendor search. Weak opportunity for three reasons. First, the market is small and Green Dot handles declarations directly, with Temu-type platforms also covering sellers. Second, the PPWR authorised-representative and producer-register rules are still unpublished (WKO, 7 Sep 2026), so the product is undefined. Third, an authorised-representative service is a legal service, not software, and Lappa and Valpak already offer it. Producers under 2 t/yr register and report but pay little. No buyer count was found.
